claims.statement: For any law P on nonempty subsets of a finite physical coordinate set, its occurrence-I-projection KL D_2(P||Q_r) equals the sum over any rooted physical partition tree of the history-conditioned child-occupancy KL divergences against the inherited global Q_r references q_v. Convexity and data processing give additive no-double-spending lower bounds from local occupancy statistics.
hypotheses: P is a probability law on nonempty subsets
Q_r is the maximum-entropy conditional-product law matching the occurrence marginals
the rooted tree recursively partitions the physical coordinates into disjoint child blocks

the one-level inherited-reference chain rule is recovered as the first split of the new arbitrary physical-tree identity

claims.statement: For depth-m recursive ternary majority, the exact occurrence KL is sum_{ell=0}^{m-1}(3/2)^ell k(u_{m,ell}), with k(u)=log2((3-3u+u^2)/4)-(3/2)log2(1-u)-(1/2)log2 u and u_{m,ell}=1-(1-c_m2^{-m})^{3^{m-ell-1}}. In particular K_occ >= (3/2)^{m-1}(m/2+log2(7/16)).
